Hi Juan / Priya —

Thanks again for the deep dive today. Wanted to capture the key pain points, goals, and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. TL;DR at the top, details below.

TL;DR
- Pain: p95 inference latency spikes hurting conversions, bursty throughput during business hours and nightly batch jobs.
- Goal: p95 <= 300ms for 256-token responses for interactive flows; sustain 40–60 rps with headroom for 100 rps bursts; US data residency and SOC2+KMS required.
- Next steps: ACME to share sample traces/payloads by EOD 11 Mar; SE design session with Dylan/Dev on 12 Mar; procurement touchpoint to start for Dedicated capacity.

Recap and notes from call
1) Pain points
 - Customer-facing agent responses: noticeable latency spikes at peak (conversions down ~4–6%).
 - Workload characteristics: mostly short instruction-following queries (~100–300 tokens response), but also periodic longer generation jobs (up to ~1k tokens) from batch processes.
 - Throughput: observed peaks today ~50–60 rps; sustained baseline ~20–30 rps.
 - Security/compliance: SOC2 required; keys via customer KMS; audit logs retention 7 years.

2) Target SLOs (customer stated)
 - Interactive flows: p95 <= 300ms for ~256 tokens (target), p99 < 800ms preferred.
 - Throughput: sustain 40–60 rps across peak window, tolerate 100 rps bursts for up to 2 minutes.
 - Availability: 99.9% monthly target for inference endpoints.

3) Model requirements
 - Quality: prefer instruction-tuned 70B model for highest quality in critical flows.
 - Cost/perf path: fall back to 13B for lower-cost/high-throughput scenarios (routing by intent).
 - Embeddings: separate embedding pipeline for search indexing; not latency-critical but throughput-heavy during nightly jobs.

4) Deployment topology (initial proposal)
 - Redwood Dedicated pool (US-west) with autoscaling and burst capacity.
 - Smart routing: route high-quality requests to 70B pool; route cost-sensitive requests to 13B; automatic fallback when capacity constrained.
 - Caching: prefix/KV cache for common prompts + warm-starting conversation contexts to reduce effective token compute.
 - Network: VPC peering + private egress; KMS for envelope encryption of keys.

Attachments: attached a draft SLO matrix & a topology sketch for reference (slo_matrix_acme_v1.xlsx, redwood_topology_v1.png).

Outstanding asks for ACME
- Sample traces, representative payloads, and 24–48h of p95/p50 telemetry (timestamps in UTC) — please send by EOD 11 Mar if possible.
- Any constraints on allowed cloud regions or IP ranges for VPC peering.
- Initial expected contract start date / procurement timeline.

Proposed next steps
1) ACME provides sample traces + payloads (due 11 Mar).
2) SE design session (60–90m) with Dylan & Dev to finalize topology and load test plan — propose Thu 12 Mar, 10:00 PT.
3) Procurement begins for Dedicated trial capacity; Redwood to provide ballpark pricing after SE session.

If that all looks right I’ll send a calendar invite for the SE session and loop in Procurement/Sales Ops. Appreciate the time today — excited to help reduce latency and cost.

Best,

Thanks for the detail, Marissa / Juan. I pulled together an initial technical approach and a couple of concrete asks so the SE session on Thu is productive.

High-level architecture (proposal)
 - Edge ingress -> Redwood routing layer -> Dedicated GPU pool(s) in us-west2 (separate pools for 13B / 70B)
 - Autoscaling policy: maintain baseline capacity for 13B to handle sustained throughput; scale 70B pool on demand with burst capacity enabled.
 - Model routing: intent classifier at request time; route to 70B for high-quality intents (billing attribution) and 13B for high-throughput intents. Automatic fallback to smaller model on overload.
 - Caching: prefix cache + KV cache for conversation context; warm caches for top ~500 prompts.

Performance tuning notes
 - Batch sizing: target dynamic batching up to 8 requests for latency-sensitive flows; larger batches for background jobs.
 - Quantization: 70B with 4-bit quantization where acceptable to reduce memory footprint; evaluate quality delta in SE session.
 - KV cache hit target: 30–40% for repeated prompts (will reduce p95 significantly).

Network & security
 - VPC peering + private egress; we can support customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key).
 - Audit logs: Redwood can export inference logs to a customer S3 bucket for SIEM ingestion.

Load test plan (what I’ll need from ACME)
 - Representative payload set (from Juan) — thanks for the sample traces; I’ll validate these.
 - Target ramp: 10k concurrent virtual users to replicate 100 rps burst window, ramp over 2 mins.
 - Success criteria: p95 <= 300ms for 256-token path under sustained 60 rps; graceful degradation to 13B path under overload.

Next asks for ACME prior to SE session
 - Confirm allowed IP ranges for VPC peering and whether AWS account IDs will be provided.
 - Provide decision matrix for which intents must always hit 70B vs which can be routed to 13B.

I attached an initial network/topology diagram (redwood_topology_v1.png) — this is a sketch we can iterate on Thu. I’ll prepare a short runbook for the load test and bring sample kernel/instance sizing recommendations (A100 80GB or H100 options).
